scope: Read-only causal audit of the currently reported immediate signed-out Store Chat error. No new browser send, server mutation, build, or release was performed.

current_truth.store_record: The canonical extension Store record says 0.2.176 Published and 0.2.205 Pending review at its latest recorded dashboard check (2026-10-04T13:16:35Z); automatic publication is enabled. The parent incident owner independently reported a fresh 13:36Z dashboard refresh with the same state. This audit did not independently refresh the dashboard.
current_truth.candidate: The submitted 0.2.205 Store ZIP was built from source 2f68bc4fef0c024f5a91d69f3c49b51c9dcd38a3; exact ZIP SHA-256 6cc56340e928376db57d31460d3c06eb894fbd0415c87b0ff372f633c5f44a26. It was tested as an unpacked copy with a public manifest key adaptation, not installed from the Store.

causal_assessment.observed_prior_failure: The earlier installed 0.2.176 reproduction sent two successful guest requests, then after panel reopen and New chat received HTTP 402 on POST /v2/ai/mandates/extend.browser_chat at 2026-10-04T05:29:10Z; the UI displayed a generic retryable error. Correlated request ID 96172141-2df1-460f-ae90-65624ae3efdc had an over-allowance guest state. Exact response bytes were not retained. Sources: .research/urgent-live-guest-20261004.json and .research/urgent-guest-server-20261004.json.
causal_assessment.candidate_fix: Current src/lib/api/stream.ts classifies HTTP 402 or 403 only if the parsed top-level error equals guest_ai_allowance_used, emits safe free-account copy and typed code; src/lib/chat/stream-error.ts removes Retry for that code. Current aidream usage_gate.py still sets HTTP 402 and a flat error envelope for a guest over limit; aidream/api/errors.py returns the envelope. The candidate therefore addresses the demonstrated 402 presentation class.
causal_assessment.candidate_runtime_proof: Independent 0.2.205 candidate native acceptance saw four fresh-guest answers, then actual offscreen HTTP 402 with flat guest_ai_allowance_used and the correct remedy without Retry. After panel reload and New chat in the same exhausted profile, a second distinct live HTTP 402 received the same correct presentation. Sources: .research/guest-402-native-acceptance.json and .research/guest-returning-final-acceptance.json.
causal_assessment.non_equivalence: A returning exhausted guest can get an immediate 402 on the first send of a new conversation; the 0.2.205 candidate proved exactly that after reload/New chat. A brand-new guest's first-ever send is a different case: the candidate fresh profile answered its first four sends before exhaustion. Neither earlier evidence identifies the reporter's present request or proves their identity is over allowance. An immediate error must be classified from its status/code rather than timing alone.
causal_assessment.server_change_boundary: Candidate native observations were at approximately 05:44-05:48Z. The live server now reports a 13:16Z build at SHA 1129ce56. Aidream source since the candidate includes tool-routing changes (bf64269d, be7f2daa, cbd614b1, 00295833) and the usage gate replacement (36af51ff); source inspection confirms the current 402 contract but does not prove current end-to-end first-send success. Earlier c01faa52 fixed a separate browser-dom InlineToolSpec schema failure that affected a first request; its source review explicitly left live guest completion unverified. This is a historical example, not attribution for the present symptom.
causal_assessment.first_request_gap: The 0.2.205 allowance native observer attached after the first completed answer and its success condition targeted later 402 responses. The recorded first answer succeeded against an earlier live server, but no first-request transport/status/error capture has been shown for the currently deployed server and the reporter's installed Store binary/profile. There is no concrete evidence in this audit of a present brand-new-guest first-send defect; it remains an acceptance gap. The pending candidate is also not yet verified as a Store installation.

next_acceptance_action: In an owned signed-out Chrome profile, first confirm the installed Store version and preserve the current profile's guest identity. Send one simple prompt on the public demo with offscreen Network and side-panel capture attached before send. Record only the first POST status, request ID/timestamp, structured error code, terminal UI outcome, and installed version; correlate the first failed request with server error surfaces/request log and deployed SHA. If it is 402 guest_ai_allowance_used on published 0.2.176, the candidate fix is applicable; after Google publishes 0.2.205, repeat on the actual Store-installed update and require the free-account remedy with no Retry. If the first request has another status/code or a stream failure, diagnose that boundary independently before claiming the 402 fix resolves the user's report.
